title: Windows: stable install-scoped aliases for --bun and run.bun
body:
# Windows: stable install-scoped aliases for --bun and run.bun

Related: [oven-sh/bun#25321](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/25321), which reports different installed and temporary Bun executables during upgrades.

## Problem

On Windows, Bun 1.4.2's `--bun` / `[run] bun = true` uses `%TEMP%\bun-node-<build SHA>\node.exe`. The installed Bun path remains stable, but the alias path changes with the Bun build. Executable-specific antivirus exceptions therefore cannot reliably follow that alias across upgrades.

The request is a stable alias per Bun installation, not a global shared alias that can switch runtimes underneath concurrent installations.

## Reproduce the path difference

Create a package with:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "runtime": "node -p \"process.execPath\""
  }
}
```

Compare `bun -e 'console.log(process.execPath)'` with `bun --bun run runtime` on Windows. The first identifies the installed Bun executable; the second uses its build-specific temporary alias. Repeat after updating Bun at the same installed path to observe the alias change. We verified released Bun's path selection and SHA-based implementation.

## Why it matters

On one Windows 11 machine with Bun 1.4.2, Vitest 5.0.0 and Bitdefender Antivirus Plus 28.0.9.198, a controlled A/B/B/A comparison of the same project test command produced:

| Condition                                      | Durations        | Worker-shutdown warnings | Tests passed per run |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------- |
| Normal ATD protection                          | 43.70 s, 43.55 s | 99, 97                   | 1,918                |
| ATD exception for the temporary node.exe alias | 8.16 s, 7.98 s   | 0, 0                     | 1,918                |

This is evidence of an ATD interaction on this machine, not proof of a Bun shutdown defect. No standalone reproduction of the antivirus slowdown has been isolated. The path churn itself is independently observable.

## Proposed fix

1. Use an alias directory tied to the stable installed executable path, rather than the build SHA. Keep separate installations separate, including concurrent versions.
2. Refresh stale Windows hard links when the installed executable is replaced. A stable directory must not retain an old runtime.
3. Share alias-path computation between creation, `NODE`/`npm_node_execpath`, and child PATH setup; preserve the original installation identity through nested Bun calls.
4. Validate existing directory/link entries and handle locked running images explicitly. Do not silently trust `ALREADY_EXISTS`.
5. Test separate simultaneous installations, an in-place replacement upgrade, nested invocations, stale aliases and unexpected existing entries.

Keep the existing temporary root and same-volume hardlink requirement. Paths then stay stable while the installation path and temporary root are unchanged. Executable paths containing unpaired UTF-16 surrogates need to survive the hash. A fix here would not by itself fix antivirus scanning performance.

With version managers such as mise and proto, selecting a new version directory would still change the alias path; this asks for one alias per installation, not one shared across managed versions.

## Current local workaround

Our project disables `run.bun` and starts package tools with a small launcher. It maintains `<installed Bun directory>\node-compat\node.exe` as a hard link and refreshes it by file identity. The launcher modifies only its child environment. Process-level tests confirm that a temporary script and its child use the same stable alias, and a replacement-file fixture confirms link refresh without changing the alias path.

After replacing the temporary-path ATD exception with the stable alias exception, the full project suite passed: 1,921 tests, 146 files, 6.33 seconds, zero worker-shutdown warnings. This verifies the local workaround; it is not a standalone reproduction of the antivirus interaction.

## Sources

- [Bun's documented run.bun behavior](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig#run-bun)
- [Bun v1.4.2 alias creation implementation](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/install/lib.rs)
- [Bun v1.4.2 run command and alias path selection](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.2/src/runtime/cli/run_command.rs)
- [Related Windows installed/temporary-runtime issue](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/25321)

bun build --compile: __dirname/__filename in an included CommonJS entrypoint are inlined as the build directory, not the $bunfs path
body:
### What happens

When a CommonJS file is included in a `bun build --compile` binary as an extra entrypoint, `__dirname` and `__filename` in that module are replaced at build time with string literals of the **build machine's** directory (`var __dirname = "/private/tmp/.../chunks";` is visible in the embedded source). Code that loads siblings via `require(path.join(__dirname, "x.cjs"))` therefore fails once the binary runs anywhere the build directory doesn't exist. `require("./x.cjs")` and `require.resolve("./x.cjs")` (→ `/$bunfs/root/chunks/x.js`) work.

### Repro (Bun 1.4.2, macOS arm64)

`app.js`
```js
const name = "loader";
require("./chunks/" + name + ".js").load("n1");
```
`chunks/loader.js`
```js
const path = require("path");
console.log("__dirname:", __dirname);
exports.load = (name) => {
  try { console.log("relative:", require("./" + name + ".cjs")); } catch (e) { console.log("relative FAIL:", e.message); }
  try { console.log("join(__dirname):", require(path.join(__dirname, name + ".cjs"))); } catch (e) { console.log("join FAIL:", e.message); }
  console.log("require.resolve:", require.resolve("./" + name + ".cjs"));
};
```
`chunks/n1.cjs`
```js
module.exports = "n1 loaded";
```
`build.js`
```js
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["app.js", "chunks/loader.js", "chunks/n1.cjs"],
  compile: { outfile: "out" },
  root: ".", naming: "[dir]/[name].[ext]", format: "cjs",
});
```
```sh
bun build.js
mv "$PWD" "$PWD.moved"      # simulate another machine: build dir no longer exists
cp "$PWD.moved/out" /tmp/empty/ && cd / && /tmp/empty/out
```
Output:
```
__dirname: /private/tmp/bun-repros/dirname-inlined/chunks
relative: n1 loaded
join FAIL: Cannot find module '/private/tmp/bun-repros/dirname-inlined/chunks/n1.cjs'
Require stack:
- /$bunfs/root/chunks/loader.js
require.resolve: /$bunfs/root/chunks/n1.js
```
Same with `format: "esm"` (`__dirname` still inlined to the build dir). Note `eval("__dirname")` in the module sees the same inlined value, since it is a module-scope variable.

| Expression inside the included CJS module | Result in the relocated binary |
|---|---|
| `__dirname` / `__filename` | build directory (wrong) |
| `require("./n1.cjs")` | works |
| `require.resolve("./n1.cjs")` | `/$bunfs/root/chunks/n1.js` (right) |
| `require(path.join(__dirname, "n1.cjs"))` | fails: build path not found |

Also noticed: `.cjs`/`.mjs` entrypoints are embedded as `.js` and the resolver maps `x.cjs` → `x.js`.

### Expected

`__dirname`/`__filename` for a module embedded in the executable should be the `/$bunfs/root/<dir>` path, consistent with `require.resolve`, rather than a path from the machine that ran the build.

### Why it matters

Bundlers' server runtimes (webpack/turbopack chunk loaders, Next.js server) load chunks with `require(path.join(__dirname, "chunks", id))`. A compiled binary that ships such chunks as extra entrypoints can't be moved off the build machine.

### Possible fix

Don't inline `__dirname`/`__filename` for modules that go into a compiled executable; leave them bound at runtime to the `$bunfs` location (or emit the `$bunfs` path).

Only Bun 1.4.2 tested; canary not tested.

title: Bun.serve sends an empty body for a file on procfs or cgroupfs (st_size 0)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (and main at 36cd1514ec)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const path = "/proc/version";
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 0,
  routes: {
    "/route": new Response(Bun.file(path)),
    "/dir/*": { dir: "/proc" },
  },
  fetch: () => new Response(Bun.file(path)),
});
for (const url of ["/handler", "/route", "/dir/version"]) {
  const res = await fetch(new URL(url, server.url));
  const body = await res.text();
  console.log(url, res.status, "content-length:", res.headers.get("content-length"), "body bytes:", body.length);
}
console.log("Bun.file(path).text() bytes:", (await Bun.file(path).text()).length);
server.stop(true);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Each response has the 219 bytes of the file, the same bytes that `Bun.file(path).text()` returns.

### What do you see instead?

```
/handler 200 content-length: 0 body bytes: 0
/route 200 content-length: 0 body bytes: 0
/dir/version 200 content-length: 0 body bytes: 0
Bun.file(path).text() bytes: 219
```

### Additional information

A regular file on procfs or cgroupfs reports `st_size` 0. The kernel makes the content at `read`. Three places in `Bun.serve` take `st_size` as the length of the body:

- `RequestContext::do_sendfile` in `src/runtime/server/RequestContext.rs`: a `BunFile` body from a `fetch` handler.
- `FileRoute::serve` in `src/runtime/server/FileRoute.rs`: a static route.
- `DirectoryRoute::on` in `src/runtime/server/DirectoryRoute.rs`: a `{ dir }` route.

The report comes from a read of the code. No user reported it before. `new Response(await Bun.file(path).bytes())` sends the bytes today.

This issue tracks the parts:

- [ ] A body that ends inside the read buffer of the server, sent with its `Content-Length`: #43974.
- [ ] A larger body. It needs a response with no `Content-Length`, and `FileResponseStream` can end one only after #37082.
- [ ] A `BunFile` that holds a size of 0 already, after `file.size` or `await file.exists()`. The cause is in `Blob::resolve_size`: #43871, #43897, #43910.
- [ ] `HEAD` from a `fetch` handler: #41585.

Not part of this issue:

- A sysfs attribute file reports `st_size` 4096 and holds fewer bytes. #41622 covers a body that ends short of its `Content-Length`.
- `respondWithFile` of `node:http2` frames from `stat.size` too: #41516.

title: bun build --compile: an embedded native addon is extracted alone, so a shared library next to it is not found (Library not loaded: @rpath/...)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A native addon that links a shared library sitting next to it works with `bun app.js` but fails inside a `--compile` binary, even when the library is embedded too. Bun extracts only the `.node` file to a temp path, so the addon's `@loader_path` rpath points at the temp directory and the library is not there.

```sh
mkdir -p lib
echo 'int foo(void) { return 42; }' > foo.c
cat > addon.c <<'C'
typedef struct napi_env__* napi_env; typedef struct napi_value__* napi_value;
int napi_create_int32(napi_env, int, napi_value*);
int napi_set_named_property(napi_env, napi_value, const char*, napi_value);
int foo(void);
napi_value napi_register_module_v1(napi_env env, napi_value exports) {
  napi_value v; napi_create_int32(env, foo(), &v);
  napi_set_named_property(env, exports, "answer", v); return exports;
}
C
clang -dynamiclib foo.c -o lib/libfoo.dylib -install_name @rpath/libfoo.dylib
clang -bundle addon.c -o lib/addon.node -undefined dynamic_lookup -Llib -lfoo -Wl,-rpath,@loader_path
echo 'const addon = require("./lib/addon.node"); console.log("answer =", addon.answer);' > app.js

bun app.js                         # answer = 42
bun build --compile app.js --asset lib --outfile app
mkdir -p elsewhere && cp app elsewhere/ && cd elsewhere && ./app
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`answer = 42`, since `lib/libfoo.dylib` is embedded next to `lib/addon.node`.

### What do you see instead?

```
error: dlopen(/var/folders/.../T/.bun-501-30ee32b4785a299.node, 0x0001): Library not loaded: @rpath/libfoo.dylib
  Referenced from: <...> /private/var/folders/.../T/.bun-501-30ee32b4785a299.node
  Reason: tried: '/private/var/folders/.../T/libfoo.dylib' (no such file), '/private/var/folders/.../T/libfoo.dylib' (no such file)
 code: "ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED"
```

`Bun.embeddedFiles` shows both `lib/addon.node` and `lib/libfoo.dylib` in the binary, so the library is there; it just is not written out next to the addon.

### Additional information

Copying the embedded directory out with its layout and loading from there works:

```js
import fs from "node:fs"; import os from "node:os"; import path from "node:path";
const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "addon-"));
for (const f of ["addon.node", "libfoo.dylib"]) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, f), fs.readFileSync("/$bunfs/root/lib/" + f));
const m = { exports: {} }; process.dlopen(m, path.join(dir, "addon.node"));
console.log("answer =", m.exports.answer); // answer = 42
```

The real-world case is sharp. Its prebuilt addon `@img/sharp-darwin-arm64/lib/sharp-darwin-arm64-0.35.4.node` has rpaths like `@loader_path/../../sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64/lib` and needs `libvips-cpp.8.18.6.dylib` from the sibling package. With both `@img` directories embedded via `--asset`, loading the addon from `/$bunfs` fails the same way:

```
dlopen(/private/tmp/.bun-501-5017f84cf75b807c.node, 0x0001): Library not loaded: @rpath/libvips-cpp.8.18.6.dylib
```

and copying the whole `@img` tree out (keeping the layout) before `process.dlopen` works. The cost is writing about 18 MB to disk at startup, which is noticeable on every cold start of a fresh container.

A fix could be to extract the addon into a temp directory that mirrors its embedded location and also write the embedded files it can reach through its rpath, or more simply every embedded file under the addon's `--asset` directory. Only tested on macOS; on Linux the equivalent would be `$ORIGIN` rpaths and `.so` files, which I would expect to fail the same way but have not checked.

Related: #15374 (sharp in a compiled binary, from the angle of embedding it at all) and #37102 (touches the same temp-file extraction).

title: bun build --compile --asset keeps only the last path segment, but --help says it preserves the relative path
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun build --help` describes `--asset` as:

```
--asset=<val>   Embed a file or directory into the compiled executable, preserving its relative path (requires --compile)
```

but only the last segment of the given path is kept. The leading directories are dropped.

```sh
mkdir -p a/b/c && echo hi > a/b/c/x.txt && echo top > a/b/y.txt
cat > app.js <<'JS'
import fs from "node:fs";
console.log(Bun.embeddedFiles.map((f) => f.name));
for (const p of ["/$bunfs/root/a/b/c/x.txt", "/$bunfs/root/b/c/x.txt", "/$bunfs/root/c/x.txt"])
  console.log(p, fs.existsSync(p));
JS
bun build --compile --asset a/b app.js --outfile app1 && ./app1
bun build --compile --asset a/b/c app.js --outfile app2 && ./app2
bun build --compile --asset ./a app.js --outfile app3 && ./app3
```

Output:

```
# --asset a/b
[ "b/c/x.txt", "b/y.txt" ]
/$bunfs/root/a/b/c/x.txt false
/$bunfs/root/b/c/x.txt true
/$bunfs/root/c/x.txt false

# --asset a/b/c
[ "c/x.txt" ]
/$bunfs/root/a/b/c/x.txt false
/$bunfs/root/b/c/x.txt false
/$bunfs/root/c/x.txt true

# --asset ./a
[ "a/b/c/x.txt", "a/b/y.txt" ]
/$bunfs/root/a/b/c/x.txt true
...
```

A single file behaves the same way: `--asset a/b/y.txt` embeds `y.txt`. An absolute path (`--asset $PWD/a/b`) also gives `b/...`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Either the help text matches the behaviour, or the relative path is kept as described, so `--asset dist/client` ends up at `/$bunfs/root/dist/client/...`.

### What do you see instead?

The asset lands at `/$bunfs/root/<basename>/...`. That matches the rule stated in #36302 ("embeds every regular file at `/$bunfs/root/<basename-of-path>/<relative-path>`"), so this may be intended, and then it is only the help text (and docs, if they say the same) that is wrong.

### Additional information

Where this bites: a server that computes paths relative to its build output (for example `path.join(outDir, "client", file)` with `outDir = "dist"`) works on disk but not in the binary, because `--asset dist/client` becomes `client/`, not `dist/client/`. The workaround is to point the app at `/$bunfs/root` as the output directory, which works but is surprising given the help text.

Two directories with the same basename are merged (`--asset a/b --asset x/b` puts both under `b/`), and only an identical file path errors with `asset "x/b" collides with another embedded file at "b/y.txt"`. That is fine, but it is another reason the naming rule should be written down.

If keeping the full relative path is off the table because it would break existing users, a way to choose the mount name would also solve it, e.g. `--asset dist/client=dist/client` or an `--asset-root` flag.

title: bun build --compile: an --external package is resolved from process.cwd(), not from the executable's directory
body:
### What happens

A compiled executable that leaves a package external (`--external dep`) finds that package only when the **current working directory** has it (or `NODE_PATH` points at it). Placing `node_modules/dep` next to the executable does nothing; running the binary from any other directory fails:

```
error: Cannot find package 'dep' from '/$bunfs/root/app'
```

`import.meta.resolve("dep")` from inside the binary reports the same, and `import.meta.dir` is `/$bunfs/root`, so the resolver walks up from the virtual path and then falls back to the cwd.

### Minimal repro (Bun 1.4.2, macOS arm64)

```
mkdir -p ext/node_modules/dep && cd ext
cat > node_modules/dep/package.json <<'EOF'
{ "name": "dep", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "module", "exports": "./index.js" }
EOF
echo 'export default "dep-loaded";' > node_modules/dep/index.js
cat > main.js <<'EOF'
import dep from "dep";
console.log("static:", dep);
EOF
bun build --compile --external dep ./main.js --outfile ./app
```

| where the binary runs | result |
|---|---|
| `./app` in `ext/` (cwd has `node_modules`) | `static: dep-loaded` |
| copy `app` **and** `node_modules` to `/somewhere/`, run `cd / && /somewhere/app` | `Cannot find package 'dep' from '/$bunfs/root/app'` |
| binary in a dir **without** `node_modules`, run with cwd = `ext/` | `static: dep-loaded` |
| any cwd, `NODE_PATH=/somewhere/node_modules` | `static: dep-loaded` |

Same result for a dynamic `await import(name)`, and with `--bytecode --format=esm --minify`. `--compile-autoload-package-json` does not change it.

The executables docs say that a relative path to a file that was not included is loaded "relative to the process's current working directory"; bare package specifiers evidently follow the same rule, and nothing in the search order looks at the executable's own directory.

### Why it matters

The natural way to ship a compiled app with optional native or heavy dependencies is `app` + `node_modules/` in one directory, started by a service manager or a container `ENTRYPOINT` whose cwd is elsewhere. Today that layout only works with `NODE_PATH` or a `cd`. The same applies to plugin systems that load packages by name at runtime, and to bundles produced by other tools that emit `createRequire(import.meta.url)("pkg")`.

### Proposal

For modules that live inside `$bunfs`, resolve bare specifiers in this order: the bundled graph → `dirname(process.execPath)/node_modules` (and its parents) → `NODE_PATH` → cwd. That is what `bun run` would do if it had been started next to the binary, and it makes `--external` under `--compile` mean "resolve at runtime next to the executable". It would also give #11732's `--include` a clean division of labour: `--include` for "put it in the binary", the execPath fallback for "leave it beside the binary".

If you would rather not change the default, a flag (`--compile-resolve-from-executable`) would do; I'm happy to send a PR either way. Related: #11732.

title: bun:test toMatchSnapshot() creates multi-megabyte files when snapshotting JSDOM nodes
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

### What platform is your computer?

MacOS

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Steps to Reproduce:

    Initialize a basic bun project and install jsdom.

    Write a test using bun:test that mounts a simple DOM node (e.g., a DocumentFragment).

    Call expect(node).toMatchSnapshot().

    Run bun test.

    Open the generated __snapshots__ directory and check the file size.



Actual Behavior:
Bun recursively walks and serializes the entire JSDOM internal object graph (including Symbol(impl)). This causes a transient memory spike and dumps hundreds of thousands of lines (often 5MB+) into a single snapshot file.

### What is the expected behavior?

Bun should serialize and print only the relevant HTML markup of the DOM node (mirroring Jest's behavior), resulting in a small snapshot file.

### What do you see instead?

Bun recursively walks and serializes the entire JSDOM internal object graph (including Symbol(impl)). This causes a transient memory spike and dumps hundreds of thousands of lines (often 5MB+) into a single snapshot file.

### Additional information

Description:

    OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)

    Bun Version: 1.4.2+744846f84

Search & Context:

    Search Terms Used: "bun test toMatchSnapshot jsdom", "massive snapshot DOM"

    Closest Existing Issue: Issue #5540

Bun.Image: decode HEIC/HEIF on Linux (dlopen system libheif)
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`Bun.Image` decodes HEIC/HEIF only through the system backends (ImageIO on macOS, WIC on Windows). On Linux there is no system backend (`HAS_SYSTEM_BACKEND` is false, per `src/runtime/image/README.md`), so HEIC input fails:

```ts
// Bun 1.4.2, oven/bun:1.4.2-slim (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64)
const bytes = await Bun.file("photo.heic").bytes(); // straight from an iPhone
await new Bun.Image(bytes).metadata();
// error: ERR_IMAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED
```

The same code works on macOS. Most servers run Linux, and HEIC is the default photo format on iPhones, so apps that accept user photo uploads work in development and break in production. Today the only option on Linux is to shell out to `heif-dec` (libheif) before `Bun.Image`, or to pull in sharp.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Decode HEIC/HEIF on Linux by `dlopen`-ing the system libheif when it is installed, the same approach #30204 proposes for AVIF via libavif. Decode-only is enough for the upload use case; if libheif isn't present, keep returning `ERR_IMAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`. Since the library is provided by the user's system (e.g. `apt install libheif1`), Bun doesn't have to bundle an HEVC decoder.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Shelling out to `heif-dec` from `libheif-examples`, then feeding the PNG to `Bun.Image` (what we do now).

title: `bun test` exits 0 and silently skips a nonexistent `./`-prefixed path when another path matches
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.13

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (baseline)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

In an empty directory containing a single test file:

```ts
// a.test.ts
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
test("a", () => { expect(1).toBe(1); });
```

run:

```sh
bun test ./a.test.ts ./missing.test.ts
echo "exit=$?"
```

`missing.test.ts` does not exist.

### What is the expected behavior?

A non-zero exit (or at minimum a warning) reporting that `./missing.test.ts` does not exist.

Bun's own diagnostic describes the `./` prefix as the way to pass an argument as a **path** rather than a filter. Running `bun test ./missing.test.ts` on its own exits 1 and prints:

```
note: To treat the "missing.test.ts" filter as a path, run "bun test ./missing.test.ts"
```

So a `./`-prefixed argument that names a file which doesn't exist should be an error in the mixed case too.

### What do you see instead?

```
 1 pass
 0 fail
 1 expect() calls
Ran 1 test across 1 file. [10.00ms]
exit=0
```

The nonexistent path is dropped silently and the run exits 0. The same happens without the `./` prefix whenever at least one other argument matches a file. If *every* argument matches nothing, `bun test` does exit 1, so the silent case is specifically a mix of present and missing paths.

### Additional information

This produces false greens in CI. A command that lists specific test files keeps passing after one of those files is renamed or deleted, and nothing reports that the named suite never ran. Scripts that pass an explicit file list are relying on each listed file actually running, so a silent skip hides lost coverage.

title: `Bun.write` stringifies input it does not support, so `Bun.write(path, img.png())` writes "[object Image]" and reports success
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+09bb54630

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.2.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts
// 1x1 RGBA PNG, so the repro needs no files on disk.
const png = Uint8Array.fromBase64(
  "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR4nGP4z8DwHwAFAAH/iZk9HQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==",
);
const img = new Bun.Image(png);

const n = await Bun.write("out.png", img.png());
console.log(n, await Bun.file("out.png").text()); // 14 "[object Image]"
```

The same thing happens for any object `Bun.write` doesn't recognise:

| call | returns | file contents |
|---|--:|---|
| `Bun.write(path, img.png())` | 14 | `[object Image]` |
| `Bun.write(path, img)` | 14 | `[object Image]` |
| `Bun.write(path, {})` | 15 | `[object Object]` |
| `Bun.write(path, new Response(img.png()))` | 70 | the PNG |
| `img.png().write(path)` | 70 | the PNG |
| `Bun.write(path, await img.png().blob())` | 70 | the PNG |

### What is the expected behavior?

A `TypeError` for input `Bun.write` can't write. `bun-types` already rejects the call (`TS2769: No overload matches this call` on `Bun.write("a.png", img.png())`), and Node's `fs.writeFile(path, {})` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`.

Separately, it might be worth accepting `Bun.Image` directly. `docs/runtime/image.mdx` says `new Response(img)` works and that `.write()` takes "the same destinations as `Bun.write`", so reaching for `Bun.write(path, img.png())` is a natural guess.

### What do you see instead?

The object is coerced with `String()`, the 14-byte string is written, and the promise resolves with 14. Nothing fails, so the bad file only turns up when something tries to decode it.

### Additional information

I ran into this in a JavaScript script, where the types can't catch it. `img.png()` reads like it returns encoded bytes, and it actually returns the `Image` with its output format set.

I used an AI assistant (Claude) to reduce this to a minimal repro and draft the issue. I ran the snippet and checked every row of the table myself.

title: prompt() returns null on a bare Enter when no default is given, so it cannot be told apart from end of input
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (744846f84), macOS arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
bun -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(prompt("Q?")))'
```

Press Enter without typing anything.

### What is the expected behavior?

`""`, the empty string the person responded with.

The HTML standard declares `prompt(optional DOMString message = "", optional DOMString default = "")`, so an omitted default is the empty string, and step 8 ("Let result be null if the user aborts, or otherwise the string that the user responded with") returns it. Browsers return `""` here.

### What do you see instead?

`null`, the same value as pressing Ctrl-D or closing standard input.

`src/runtime/webcore/prompt.rs` sets `default` to `JSValue::NULL` when the second argument is missing, and returns `default` when the first byte read is a newline.

### Additional information

A script that asks "Press Enter to continue, or Ctrl-D to stop" cannot use `prompt` to tell the two answers apart. Passing a default works around it, but prints the default in brackets after the question. We read one line from `console` instead.

title: `bun update <pkg>` does not re-resolve packages whose `$pkg` override changed; lock stays stale and `bun install` / `--frozen-lockfile` do not notice
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (744846f84)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0 x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This setup uses a `$name` override where the overridden package is only a transitive dependency and is not the package being referenced:

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
cat > package.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "repro",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "artillery-engine-playwright": "1.27.0",
    "playwright": "1.62.1"
  },
  "overrides": {
    "@playwright/test": "$playwright"
  }
}
EOF
export PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1
bun install --ignore-scripts                  # @playwright/test@1.62.1, as expected
sed -i 's/"playwright": "1.62.1"/"playwright": "^1.62.1"/' package.json
bun install --ignore-scripts

bun update playwright --ignore-scripts        # playwright 1.62.1 -> 1.63.0
grep '"@playwright/test' bun.lock | cut -c1-80
```

`artillery-engine-playwright@1.27.0` depends on `@playwright/test: 1.58.1`, so the only reason it gets `@playwright/test@1.62.1` is the override.

### What is the expected behavior?

After `playwright` moves to 1.63.0, `$playwright` means `^1.63.0`, so `@playwright/test` should be re-resolved to 1.63.0.

### What do you see instead?

Bun updates the overrides section of `bun.lock` but leaves the resolved package at 1.62.1:

```
  "overrides": {
    "@playwright/test": "^1.63.0",
  },
...
    "@playwright/test": ["@playwright/test@1.62.1", ...
    "@playwright/test/playwright": ["playwright@1.62.1", ...
    "@playwright/test/playwright/playwright-core": ["playwright-core@1.62.1", ...
```

The lock is now inconsistent with its own overrides section, but no command fixes it:

- a later `bun install` reports `no changes`
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes
- `bunx --bun playwright --version` prints `1.62.1`, because `@playwright/test` owns `node_modules/.bin/playwright`

Things that do produce `@playwright/test@1.63.0`:

- deleting `bun.lock` and running `bun install`
- `bun update playwright @playwright/test`
- using a literal override instead of `$playwright`: changing `"@playwright/test": "1.62.1"` to `"1.63.0"` and running `bun install` re-resolves it correctly

So the problem only happens when the value of a `$ref` override changes.

### Additional information

Real-world impact: we use this override so artillery's transitive Playwright follows our direct `playwright` dependency. After a routine `bun update playwright`, our Docker image's `bunx --bun playwright install` baked the old browsers (1.62.1). Every test then failed with `Executable doesn't exist at .../chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`.

Related: #31748 (a self-referencing `$vite` override leaving a stale nested copy), which was closed as a duplicate of #13388 and reported fixed by #38333. That fix is included in 1.4.2. The case here is different: the overridden package (`@playwright/test`) is not the referenced one (`playwright`) and is not a direct dependency, and a follow-up `bun install` does not fix it.

title: node:http2: stream.state.localWindowSize never changes
fs.watch on macOS: three differences from libuv in how FSEvents events are filtered
body:
### What happens

On macOS, `FSEventsLoop::events_cb` in `src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs` decides which FSEvents events a watcher reports. It differs from libuv's `uv__fsevents_event_cb` in three cases:

1. An event with a system flag is reported as a `change` of the watched directory. libuv reports nothing.
2. The removal of the watched directory is not reported. libuv 1.49.0 and later reports `rename`.
3. A non-recursive watcher on `/` reports nothing. libuv reports a direct child as `/name`.

Found during the work on #43923. That PR does not change these.

**These are not observed at runtime.** I have no macOS machine. They come from reading the code next to libuv, and from a copy of both filters that I ran over 1680 combinations of watched path, event path, recursion and flags.

### Cause

1. libuv drops every event that carries `UserDropped`, `KernelDropped`, `EventIdsWrapped`, `HistoryDone`, `Mount`, `Unmount` or `RootChanged` ([fsevents.c#L249-L251](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/v1.52.0/src/unix/fsevents.c#L249-L251)). `events_cb` has no such check. An event of this kind names the watched path and has no `ItemIsDir` flag. So `is_file` is true ([fs_events.rs#L551](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4227e466c489/src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs#L551)), the empty remainder takes the basename branch, and the watcher reports `change` with the name of the watched directory.
2. An event whose path equals the watched directory is dropped ([fs_events.rs#L557-L560](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4227e466c489/src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs#L557-L560)). libuv removed the same check in 1.49.0 ("fsevents: detect watched directory removal").
3. The path of a root watcher keeps its leading `/`. The subdirectory filter drops each path that contains a `/` ([fs_events.rs#L577-L583](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4227e466c489/src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs#L577-L583)). libuv starts that search after the first byte ([fsevents.c#L296-L301](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/v1.52.0/src/unix/fsevents.c#L296-L301)).

### How to check on a Mac

Item 2 has a short script. By libuv's code, a Node version with libuv 1.49.0 or later prints `rename` with the directory name. By the code above, Bun prints nothing.

```js
const fs = require("fs");
const os = require("os");
const path = require("path");

const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "watched-"));
fs.watch(dir, (event, filename) => console.log(event, filename));
setTimeout(() => fs.rmdirSync(dir), 500);
setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 1500);
```

Item 1 needs FSEvents to drop events, or a volume to mount or unmount below the watched path. I know no script that triggers it on demand.

Item 3 needs a change to a direct child of `/`.

### Practical effect

Item 1 can make a test fail that asserts the exact names a watcher reports: a loaded machine can add one event with the name of the watched directory. Item 2 is what a program sees when a watched directory goes away. Item 3 is listed for completeness.

### Numbers from the model

With #43923 applied, the copy of Bun's filter differs from the copy of libuv 1.52.0 in 286 of 1680 combinations: 174 for item 1, 20 for item 2, 20 for item 3. The other 72 need an event path or a watched path with a trailing slash. I do not expect FSEvents or `F_GETPATH` to produce one.

title: bun build: url("./C#/logo.png?v=2") does not resolve when a directory name has a literal # and the URL has a query
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (1.3.5 does the same)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir -p "C#" && head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "C#/logo.png"
printf '.a { background: url("./C#/logo.png?v=2"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The build finds `C#/logo.png` and prints `url("./logo-68tr27nb.png?v=2")`.

### What do you see instead?

```
error: Could not resolve: "./C#/logo.png?v=2"
```

`url("./C#/logo.png")` resolves, and `url("./logo.png?v=2")` resolves. The two together do not.

### Additional information

I found this when I worked on #43907. No user reported it. esbuild 0.18.6 fails the same way (`Could not resolve "./C#/logo.png?v=2"`).

For an import from CSS or HTML, the resolver tries the specifier as written. When that fails, it tries one more time without the text from the first `?` or `#` (`src/resolver/resolver.rs`, the retry for `kind.is_from_css()`). Here the first `#` is part of the directory name, so the retry looks for `./C` and gives up. A retry at each later `?` or `#` would find `./C#/logo.png` with the suffix `?v=2`.

The CSS printer puts the removed suffix back on the rewritten URL. With #43911 it reads one flag on the import record and takes the suffix from the first `?` or `#` of the specifier. A retry at a later position needs the record to carry the position of the cut, not only the flag.

title: bun build: a CSS url() to a copied asset is not loadable when the output path has a literal #, ? or %
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (1.3.5 does the same)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "icon#1.png"
printf '.a { background: url("./icon#1.png"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out
ls out && grep -o 'url([^)]*)' out/*.css
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A URL that a browser resolves to the copied file `out/icon#1-68tr27nb.png`, for example `url("./icon%231-68tr27nb.png")`.

### What do you see instead?

```
url("./icon#1-68tr27nb.png")
```

A browser ends the path at the `#` and requests `./icon`, which does not exist. (1.4.0 to 1.4.2 also append `#1.png`. That part is #43907.)

The same happens for a `?` or a `%` in the file name. It also happens for a directory name when the asset naming has `[dir]`:

```sh
mkdir -p "C#" && head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "C#/logo.png"
printf '.a { background: url("./C#/logo.png"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out --asset-naming="[dir]/[name]-[hash].[ext]"
# url("./C#/logo-68tr27nb.png")  -> a browser requests ./C
```

### Additional information

I found this when I worked on #43907. No user reported it. esbuild 0.18.6 prints the same kind of URL (`url(./icon#1-55H3Y73Q.png)`).

The output path of a copied asset replaces a placeholder in the printed chunk, as raw bytes (`IntermediateOutput::code_with_source_map_shifts`, `src/bundler/Chunk.rs`). #41793 percent-encodes that path for HTML chunks (`src` and `href`). CSS chunks go through the same join and are not covered by it.

title: bun build: a CSS url() gets part of the file path appended when a directory or file name has a literal # or ?
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (the change that causes it is in the 1.4.0, 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 tags, and main at 73df7bb270 has it too)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir -p "C#" && head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "C#/logo.png"
printf 'body { background: url("./C#/logo.png"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out
grep -o 'url([^)]*)' out/*.css
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
url("./logo-68tr27nb.png")
```

Bun 1.3.5 prints this. esbuild 0.18.6 prints `url(./logo-DFVMILRG.png)` for the same input.

### What do you see instead?

```
url("./logo-68tr27nb.png#/logo.png")
```

The text after the first `#` or `?` of the specifier is appended to the rewritten URL, although it is part of the file path.

Other shapes of the same bug:

- A small asset is inlined: `url("data:image/png;base64,...#/logo.png")`.
- A `?` in a name: `url("./what?/logo.svg")` becomes `url("./logo-<hash>.svg?/logo.svg")`.
- The dev server prints `url("/_bun/asset/<hash>.png#/logo.png")`.
- An absolute specifier under a `C#` directory, `url("/home/me/C#/proj/img/logo.svg")`, becomes `url("./logo-<hash>.svg#/proj/img/logo.svg")`. Local path segments go into the output CSS, and the bytes and the hash of the CSS chunk depend on where the project is checked out.

### Additional information

I found this when I read the code for #43854. No user reported it, and I did not find a public stylesheet that hits it. In the directory-name case the asset still loads, because a browser ignores an unknown fragment on an image. An SVG consumer that reads the fragment (`#svgView`, a `mask` or `clip-path` id) gets a fragment that the author did not write.

It is a regression from #33685, first released in 1.4.0. Before that change the CSS printer appended nothing. Since that change, `Printer::get_import_record_url` (`src/css/printer.rs`) takes the suffix from the text of the specifier: everything from the first `?` or `#`. The resolver tries the specifier as written first and removes the `?query#fragment` only when that fails (`src/resolver/resolver.rs`, the retry for `kind.is_from_css()`). For `./C#/logo.png` the first try finds the file and nothing is removed, but the printer still appends `#/logo.png`.

When node-gyp can't write its cache folder (in a sandboxed install, for example), the install fails with exit code 1 even though the package works.

No default `node-gyp rebuild` when `gypfile` is `false`, same as npm. `@npmcli/run-script` only adds it when:

```js
!scripts.install && !scripts.preinstall && gypfile !== false && await isNodeGypPackage(path)
```

### What do you see instead?

`node-gyp rebuild` runs, and the install fails if node-gyp does.

### Additional information

The places that add the default script only check for an empty `install` / `preinstall` and an existing `binding.gyp`: `src/install/lockfile/Package/Scripts.rs` (twice) and `load_root_lifecycle_scripts` in `src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerLifecycle.rs`.

For a local `file:` dependency it only shows up if the package has some other lifecycle script, such as a `postinstall`. better-sqlite3 from the registry hits it without one.

Bun.SQL: a query started in the same tick as a graceful `close()` / `end()` is rejected and never sent
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9. The code is the same on main at c8e1f6fa5b.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (the code is JavaScript in `src/js/internal/sql/`, it is the same on every platform)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No server is necessary:

```js
import { SQL } from "bun";
const sql = new SQL("sqlite://:memory:");
await sql`create table t (x)`;
const inserted = sql`insert into t values (1) returning x`.then(rows => rows[0].x);
await sql.close();
console.log(await inserted);
```

The same happens at the end of an `await using` block, because `Symbol.asyncDispose` calls `close()`:

```js
{
  await using db = new SQL({ adapter: "sqlite", filename: "data.db" });
  await db`create table if not exists t (x)`;
  for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) db`insert into t values (${i})`.catch(console.error);
}
// 20 x ERR_SQLITE_CONNECTION_CLOSED, 0 rows in data.db
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The first program prints `1`. The second program writes 20 rows.

`close()` with no timeout is a graceful close. `packages/bun-types/sql.d.ts` says "with no timeout it waits for all queries to finish first". `docs/runtime/sql.mdx` says `await sql.close(); // await all queries to finish and close all connections from the pool`. The queries above started before `close()` was called.

### What do you see instead?

The query rejects with `ERR_SQLITE_CONNECTION_CLOSED` ("Connection closed"). The statement never runs. PostgreSQL and MySQL do the same with `ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED` and `ERR_MYSQL_CONNECTION_CLOSED`. A mock server that records every statement receives nothing.

A grace period does not help. `close({ timeout: 5 })` closes at once, because it sees no pending query.

Results for a query that starts before `close()` in the same tick, on the three adapters:

| Start of the query | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `q.then(...)`, `q.catch(...)`, `q.finally(...)`, `q.run()` | rejected, never sent |
| `q.execute()` | runs, `close()` waits for it |
| `await q` in an async function that the caller does not await | rejected, never sent |

The same program with `close()` one macrotask later drains correctly. So the documented contract depends on a microtask order that the caller cannot see.

### Additional information

A `Query` is lazy. `then()`, `catch()`, `finally()` and `run()` go through `#runAsync()` in `src/js/internal/sql/query.ts`, which does `await Promise.$resolve()` before it gives the query to the pool. So the pool learns about the query one promise job after the caller started it. `BaseSQLAdapter.close()` in `src/js/internal/sql/shared.ts` sets `closed = true` and reads `hasPendingQueries()` once, synchronously. It sees nothing and closes. `SQLiteAdapter.close()` closes the database synchronously. The late query then reaches `connect()`, which rejects it because the pool is closed.

The lazy `Query` comes from postgres.js. There, `Query.handle()` has the same one-job delay (`await 1`), and `sql.end()` starts with a matching `await 1` before it marks the pool as ending. Bun has the first half and not the second. With postgres 3.3.5 against a local PostgreSQL, on Node.js and on Bun:

| Program | postgres.js | Bun.SQL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `q.then(r => r); await sql.end()` | resolves | rejects, never sent |
| `q.then(r => r); await sql.end({ timeout: 5 })` | resolves | rejects, never sent |
| `q.execute(); await sql.end()` | resolves | resolves |
| `sql.end(); q.then(r => r)` (query starts after `end()`) | rejects | rejects |
| async function with `await q`, not awaited, then `sql.end()` | rejects | rejects |

The Bun port of the postgres.js test "Connection end does not cancel query" first needed an `await 1` before `sql.end()` (#16512). #16854 removed it when `.execute()` became synchronous. The other ways to start a query kept the race.

A change in `Query` alone does not fix this. #33740 tried a synchronous hand-off in `then()`. It did not cover `await q`, it sent a query started inside `onclose` to a dead connection, and it changed `q.then(); q.cancel()` from "cancelled, nothing sent" to "sent". That part was removed from #33740, and its notes leave the question to a fix in `close()`.

A workaround is `q.execute()` before the `then()`, or `await null` before `close()`. An early `return` or a `throw` out of an `await using` block skips the second one.

Bun Shell: `for`, `while` and other unsupported reserved words run as commands, and the loop body runs once
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9 (also main at 6d504dd983)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (the code path is platform independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
import { $ } from "bun";

const f = await $`for f in one two three; do
  echo "f=[$f]"
done`.nothrow().quiet();
console.log(JSON.stringify(f.stdout.toString()), f.exitCode);

const w = await $`while false; do
  echo BODY
done
echo tail`.nothrow().quiet();
console.log(JSON.stringify(w.stdout.toString()), w.exitCode);
```

The same happens in a `.sh` file that `bun run` executes. A one-line loop (`for f in a b; do echo $f; done`) does not run its body, because `do echo $f` is one command named `do`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Bun Shell does not support `for`, `while`, `until`, `case`, `select` or `function`. A script that uses one of them must fail before it runs a command, the way `echo hi &` fails today with `Background commands "&" are not supported yet.`

### What do you see instead?

```
"f=[]\n" 1
"BODY\ntail\n" 0
```

stderr has `bun: command not found: for`, `bun: command not found: do` and `bun: command not found: done`. The shell looks up each reserved word as a command, reports that it does not exist, and continues with the next statement. So each line of the loop body runs once as a plain command, with the loop variable empty. The body of `while false` runs, and the script exits 0.

This can lose data. `for f in a b c; do rm -rf "$dir/$f"; done` runs `rm -rf "$dir/"` once.

### Additional information

- `parse_compound_cmd` (`src/shell_parser/parse.rs:969`) special-cases only `(`, `if` and `[[`. Every other word goes to `parse_simple_cmd`, which takes `for`, `do` and `done` as command names.
- #36196 was an earlier fix: a parse error for these words in command position, with quoted and interpolated words left alone. It was closed as stale, with no review from a maintainer.
- Today a tab-indented loop body does not run, because the lexer does not split words on a tab and each body line fails with `command not found: \trm`. When the lexer splits on a tab, a tab-indented body behaves like a space-indented body, and this bug reaches it too.

title: Bun Shell: the output of a command substitution is not split on a tab
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9 (also main at 6d504dd983)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (the code path is platform independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
import { $ } from "bun";
await $`echo $(printf 'a\tb\tc')`;
```

### What is the expected behavior?

bash and dash print `a b c`. The output of an unquoted command substitution is split into fields on the default `IFS`: space, tab and newline. `echo` gets three arguments.

### What do you see instead?

```
a	b	c
```

`echo` gets one argument that contains the two tabs. Tab-separated output from tools like `cut`, `awk` or `git` does not split into words.

### Additional information

- `post_subshell_expansion` (`src/runtime/shell/states/Expansion.rs:548`) turns each newline into a space and then splits on runs of `b' '` only (lines 579 and 585). A tab is never a separator there.
- Do not add the tab to that loop before the operands of `[[ ]]` stop being split. `CondExpr` expands each operand with the same splitting expansion (`src/runtime/shell/states/CondExpr.rs:69`). `[[ -f $(echo 'my file') ]]` is false in Bun today and true in bash, because the operand is split on the space. `[[ -f $(printf 'my\tfile') ]]` is true today only because a tab does not split. A tab split alone makes that case false too.
- #33552 was an earlier attempt. It made the split follow `IFS`. It was closed as stale, with no review from a maintainer.
- The lexer has the same gap for a tab in the script text. That part has its own fix and does not touch this layer.

title: node:http default agent reuses a socket after a Connection: close request in 1.4.2 (every second request ECONNRESET/EPIPE)
Bun.serve: send Keep-Alive: timeout=<idleTimeout> by default (like node:http)
body:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`Bun.serve` keeps HTTP/1.1 connections alive and closes idle ones after `idleTimeout` (default 10 s), but by default it does not tell the client about that deadline: responses carry no `Keep-Alive: timeout=…` header.

Clients that pool connections (`http.Agent`, undici, most language HTTP stacks) use that header to retire a pooled socket *before* the server closes it. Without it, a client can reuse a socket at the moment the server is closing it for idleness, and that request fails with `ECONNRESET` / `socket hang up`. Nothing is logged on the server side. This is rare, because it needs a reuse that lands on the idle deadline, but it cannot be prevented from the client side.

`node:http` sends the header by default, and so does `node:http` running under Bun:

```js
// a.mjs: Bun.serve
Bun.serve({ port: 3111, fetch: () => new Response("ok") });
// b.mjs: node:http (run with `bun b.mjs` or `node b.mjs`)
require("node:http").createServer((_, res) => res.end("ok")).listen(3112);
```

Raw response headers for one `GET / HTTP/1.1` on Bun 1.4.2:

```
Bun.serve              -> content-type, Date, Content-Length
node:http (under bun)  -> Date, Connection: keep-alive, Keep-Alive: timeout=5, Content-Length
```

As noted in #25566, you can already set the header yourself, and Bun passes it through to the wire. I confirmed this on 1.4.2:

```js
Bun.serve({ fetch: () => new Response("ok", { headers: { "Keep-Alive": "timeout=9" } }) });
```

So this is not a bug report. The ask is about the default: every app has to know to add a header whose correct value depends on its own `idleTimeout`, and most won't.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

On keep-alive HTTP/1.1 responses, send `Keep-Alive: timeout=<idleTimeout>` by default, matching `node:http`. Keep the current behaviour when the handler sets its own `Keep-Alive` or `Connection` header, and when `idleTimeout` is `0` (disabled).

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Setting the header in every handler, which is what we do today. It works, but it's easy to miss, and the value has to be kept in sync with `idleTimeout` by hand.
- A client-side pool idle timeout shorter than the server's. That requires every client to know the server's setting.

`JSValue::to_int32()` reads a non-number through `asInt32()`: an assertion in debug builds, unrelated bits in release builds
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

Main at 6d504dd983 (read of the code). The example below ran on 1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9.

### What platform is your computer?

All platforms. The code is not platform specific.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`JSValue::to_int32()` (`src/jsc/JSValue.rs:765`) converts an int32 and a double in Rust. Its last line, `JSC__JSValue__toInt32(self)`, runs only when the value is not a number. That shim calls `JSC::JSValue::asInt32()` (`src/jsc/bindings/bindings.cpp:4754`), which is never valid for a non-number:

- A debug build aborts: `ASSERTION FAILED: isInt32()` at `JSCJSValue.h(683) : int32_t JSC::JSValue::asInt32() const`.
- A release build returns the low 32 bits of the encoded value. `null` reads as 2, `false` as 6, `true` as 7, and a cell as the low half of its address.

`to_int64()` has the same shape. `JSC__JSValue__toInt64` asserts `isHeapBigInt() || isNumber()` and then reads `asDouble()`. `to_u32()` builds on `to_int64()`.

So each caller must check the type first, and nothing mechanical checks that it does. At 6d504dd983 there are 68 `.to_int32()` calls in 33 files, 34 `.to_int64()` calls and 27 `.to_u32()` calls. A fuzzer or an audit found each missed guard, and each got its own PR:

- merged: #28926, #32738, #39977, #39991, #41148
- open: #40773 (`bun:ffi` `read.*` offset), #41652 (`console.dir` depth), #43818 (`Bun.SQL` options), #43838 (node:cluster primary)

Example of the release behavior, from #43838: a cluster worker sends `addressType: false`. The primary reads 6, binds IPv6 for `127.0.0.1`, and replies `EINVAL`. Node replies errno 0.

This is a finding from the review of #43838. It is filed so that it has a tracker.

### What is the expected behavior?

A read of a non-number cannot reach `asInt32()` or `asDouble()`. A caller that forgets the type check gets a compile error, a lint failure, or a defined value.

### What do you see instead?

An assertion in debug builds, and unrelated bits in release builds, at each call site that has no guard.

### Additional information

Directions that came up in the review. None is decided.

- Make the fall-through total: keep a debug assertion in Rust, and return a defined value in release builds. This removes the unrelated bits. It does not remove the need for a guard where the defined value is itself valid input, for example a cluster `seq` of 0.
- Add an accessor that returns `Option<i32>` for the sites that take user values, and ban the bare call there with a `clippy.toml` `disallowed-methods` entry or a source lint.
- #42142 already moves the number to `i64` conversion into Rust.

The remaining sites without a guard that the audits listed are four `bun:internal-for-testing` helpers: `setSocketOptions`, `proxyInternals.noProxyMatches`, `internalSourceMap.find` and `linearFifoOrderedRemoveProbe`.

### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (first bad release: 1.3.12)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.1.3-100.fc43.x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const error = new Error("first");
error.stack; // read once
Error.captureStackTrace(error);
error.message = "second";
console.log(error.stack.split("\n")[0]);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`Error: second`, as in Node v25.2.1 and in Bun up to 1.3.11.

### What do you see instead?

`Error: first`

### Additional information

Once an error's `stack` has been read, `Error.captureStackTrace` on it computes the new stack at capture time instead of on the next read. The same happens with an `Error.prepareStackTrace` installed: it runs at capture.

```js
const error = new Error("first");
error.stack;
Error.prepareStackTrace = (e) => `prepared: ${e.message}`;
Error.captureStackTrace(error);
error.message = "second";
console.log(error.stack); // Node and Bun 1.3.11: "prepared: second"; Bun 1.3.12 and later: "prepared: first"
```

| Build | Output of the first repro |
|---|---|
| 1.3.11+af24e281e | `Error: second` |
| canary 2026-03-28, `44f5b6a1d` | `Error: second` |

title: bun test traps before loading tests when macOS Seatbelt denies hw.pagesize_compat
body:
### Reproduction

On macOS 26.7 (x86_64) with Bun 1.4.2, create `seatbelt-smoke.test.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
test("smoke", () => expect(1).toBe(1));
```

Then run:

```sh
sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)(deny sysctl-read (sysctl-name "hw.pagesize_compat"))' -- bun test ./seatbelt-smoke.test.ts
```

### Actual

Bun prints its test-runner banner, then panics with `Trap instruction` before loading the test (exit 133). The same test passes under `(version 1)(allow default)` and passes when an exact `(allow sysctl-read (sysctl-name "hw.pagesize_compat"))` exception is added to the restrictive profile. Other operation-class grants did not prevent the trap.

### Expected

A denied, read-only sysctl query should not crash the test runner; Bun should handle the failure gracefully or use an available fallback.

### Context

This affects running `bun test` inside a macOS sandbox. The reproducer deliberately denies only one sysctl key and otherwise allows all operations, so it is independent of project-specific filesystem/network restrictions. A narrow application-side workaround is tracked in and1truong/tabterm#206. Not yet verified on arm64.
